full_description: Research Scientist I - The Shalek Lab - - 22716 - Broad Institute Skip to content Broad Institute About Broad Careers Join Our Talent Community Login Create Profile Research Scientist I - The Shalek Lab General information Location Cambridge, MA Ref # 45142 Job Family Research Workplace On-Site Date published 10/22/2026 Time Type Full time Pay Range $88,000.00/yr - $124,000.00/yr Description & Requirements The Shalek Lab (MIT, Broad Institute, and Ragon Institute) and the Ex Vivo Project , (Broad Institute, Dana-Farber Cancer Institute, and Microsoft) are looking for a highly motivated Research Scientist I with strong computational and data science expertise, interested in learning, engineering, and targeting cell states from large-scale single-cell data. Research directions will center on a forward-engineering platform that links transcriptional cell states to function: pooled transcription factor (TF) ORF overexpression and other genetic perturbation screens read out by scRNA-seq across cancer lineages, with a focus on the cell-intrinsic programs that drive immune tolerance and therapy resistance. The core work is computational: building scalable pipelines for quality control, benchmarking, and integration of large single-cell and multi-omic datasets, and partnering with machine learning scientists to turn structured perturbation data into predictive models of cell state and fitness. The projects entail rigorous study design, large-scale data analysis and interpretation, close coordination with wet-lab team members and partners, and communication to the lab and greater scientific community. Due to the large number of datasets and the many affiliated labs and personnel, the position requires critical attention to detail, excellent communication, and time-management skills, including effective collaboration in a remote, distributed team. The position offers an opportunity to gain fundamental skills leading a team in an interdisciplinary, technology-driven environment and access to the intellectual resources of the Broad, MIT, Harvard, and Dana-Farber communities. Job Duties: The Research Scientist will lead the computational analysis and data integration efforts of the cell-state engineering platform and support the Principal Investigators and collaborators of the study. The scientist will be responsible for designing and executing analyses, maintaining reproducible data pipelines, and coordinating with experimental and machine learning collaborators, while working remotely. The role includes training and mentoring junior lab members and visiting scholars to use and extend the analysis framework. Key responsibilities: Lead the computational design and analysis of pooled TF-ORF and other perturbation screens with scRNA-seq readouts, including benchmarking, quality-control frameworks, and end-to-end analysis pipelines, to map transcriptional states to fitness and functional phenotypes. Build, document, and maintain scalable, reproducible workflows for large-scale single-cell data processing on high-performance and cloud computing infrastructure, including multiplexed sample demultiplexing and batch-effect correction. Integrate large, heterogeneous datasets (perturbation screens, bulk and single-cell RNA-seq, public cell atlases, spatial and other multi-omic data, and genomic data) to identify gene programs and regulators of cancer cell-state transitions, immune tolerance, and drug resistance. Collaborate closely with machine learning scientists to generate structured, well-annotated datasets for model training, evaluate model performance, and design experiments to validate model predictions. Communicate study findings efficiently and present data at lab, institute, and external meetings as projects progress; contribute to manuscripts and preprints. Collaborate extensively with colleagues across disciplines within the group and with external partners, including experimental biologists, computational scientists, clinicians, and industry scientists. Train, mentor, and supervise junior computational and experimental researchers, rotation students, and visiting scholars. Qualifications: Ph.D. in Bioengineering, Computational Biology, Bioinformatics, Medical Engineering, Data Science, or related quantitative fields. 4+ years of relevant research experience applying computational approaches to large-scale single-cell and multi-omic data to solve biomedical problems; familiarity with perturbation screen design and the experimental workflows that generate the data is a plus. Demonstrated experience analyzing pooled genetic perturbation screens (e.g., ORF/TF overexpression, CRISPR) with scRNA-seq readouts, including quality control, normalization, batch correction, and benchmarking. Strong time management and communication skills to balance multiple analyses between several collaborators in a remote work environment. Ability to multi-task and work independently under pressure. Ability to work in a team environment, meet deadlines, and prioritize and balance work from multiple individuals; experience mentoring junior researchers. Extensive experience integrating and analyzing multi-omics data (e.g., genetics, bulk RNA-seq, single-cell RNA-seq, spatial omics, public atlases) for biomedical research. Proficient coding/scripting in Python and R, with experience in the scientific Python ecosystem (e.g., scanpy, pandas, scikit-learn) and sound software engineering practices (version control, reproducible workflows). Experience with Linux environments, high-performance computing and/or cloud computing, and broad experience with open-source bioinformatics tools to generate biological insight from large datasets. Experience collaborating with machine learning scientists, such as preparing training datasets, benchmarking predictive models, or applying ML methods to biological data, is highly desirable. High productivity, evidenced by high-quality collaborative science and research publications in peer-reviewed journals on which they are named co-authors. The expected base pay range for this position as listed above is based on a 40 hour per week schedule. Broad provides pay ranges representing its reasonable and good faith estimate of what the organization reasonably expects to pay for a position at the time of posting. Actual compensation will vary based on factors including but not limited to, relevant skills, experience, education, qualifications, and other factors permissible by law. At Broad, your base pay is just one part of a comprehensive total rewards package. From day one, this role offers a competitive benefits package including medical, dental, vision, life, and disability insurance; a 401(k) retirement plan; flexible spending and health savings accounts; at least 13 paid holidays; winter closure; paid time off; parental and family care leave; and an employee assistance program, among other Broad benefits. The Broad Institute is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, national origin, religion, age, color, sex, disability, protected veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by local, state, or federal laws, rules, or regulations. full_description:
Outset invented a better way to do research: AI-powered user interviews.

Global brands like Hubspot, Microsoft, Uber and Nestle use Outset to achieve deeper, qualitative insights about their users at unprecedented speed and scale.

The research industry is massive (>$140B and growing) and ripe for disruption. Incumbents are outdated, slow, and burdened by high-cost services. That's our opportunity.


Outset is backed by top Silicon Valley investors and raised a $30M Series B in December 2025—less than six months after our Series A—led by Radical Ventures with participation from M12 (Microsoft’s venture arm), 8VC, Y Combinator, and Adverb Ventures.

The raise follows a breakout year, with our business growing 8x as enterprise customers across industries adopt our category, AI‑moderated research, as the new standard for understanding people.

We’re a tight-knit team serving some of the world’s largest enterprises.

Outset builds digital twins: AI systems that represent specific real people and respond to research questions the way those people would. The Digital Twins Team runs an ongoing research program to measure and improve how faithfully these systems reproduce human responses and behavior, across a range of cross-sectional levels of analysis.

The Research Scientist works directly with and reports to the Head Scientist. Together you will choose what to study, design the studies, define how results are measured, interpret the findings, and write them up for internal decision-making and, where appropriate, for academic publication. You will bring current methodological training in computational social science, data science, survey-methodology, human-computation interaction, and experiment design.

Responsibilities

  • Co-design and run studies that compare system-generated responses with responses from humans, using both qualitative and quantitative measures.

  • Design, justify, and hone measures of performance.

  • Apply and adapt state-of-the-art statistical techniques common to survey methodology and large-scale social data analysis, to benchmark and improve sample- and population-level simulation performance.

  • Design evaluations and experiments with pre-specified analysis plans.

  • Design and oversee human rating studies, including rater training, coding rubrics, and inter-rater agreement measurement.

  • Design data collection from third-party data sources and directly from human participants, including longitudinal and repeated-measures studies.

  • Contribute to the research agenda for new modeling approaches, including evaluation of fine-tuned models and of model calibration.

  • Specify analyses precisely enough for an engineer to implement.

  • Co-author papers, preprints, and presentations.

Qualifications

  • A completed or nearly completed PhD in computational social science, communication, HCI, sociology, political science, psychology, statistics, or a related field.

  • Peer-reviewed publications on which you were a primary author.

  • Working command of graduate-level statistical methodology common to social science, including the assumptions behind each.

  • Experience analyzing large-scale telemetry and behavioral datasets, with attention to the validity of the resulting inference.

  • Familiarity with machine learning, spanning classical, nonparametric, and LLM-based approaches, including how transformer-based language models work, what fine-tuning does, and how the major model families differ.

  • Fundamentals of computing: file systems, software libraries, databases, SQL, and tabular data.

  • Ability to work in an environment where most code is produced through agentic coding tools, and to read and check that code.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience fine-tuning open-weight language models on survey, experimental, or behavioral data.

  • Experience building or evaluating calibrated confidence or error-prediction models, including deriving decision thresholds from human judgments.

  • Experience measuring similarity of open-ended text, for example with embedding-based methods.

  • Experience designing or running panel-based data collection with human participants.

  • Experience presenting research at academic and/or industry conferences.

  • Prior work on generative agents, digital twins, or simulation of human respondents.

  • Familiarity with the startup ecosystem

  • Familiarity with qualitative interviews and ethnographic methods

  • Familiarity with topics in computational linguistics
